extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners; patent prosecutors and attorneys
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for patent examiners (and useful to practitioners) on grounds for rejecting claims and procedural/form requirements when issuing Office actions (e.g., 35 U.S.C. 112 rejections, duplicate claim objections, new matter, foreign filing bars, final rejection practice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential Elements Omitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, as being incomplete for omitting essential elements, such omission amounting to a gap between the elements. The omitted elements are: [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rejection must be preceded by form paragraph 7.30.02. Examiner must give the rationale for considering the omitted elements critical or essential and recite the elements omitted from the claims in bracketed text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential Cooperative Relationships Omitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, as being incomplete for omitting essential structural cooperative relationships of elements, such omission amounting to a gap between the necessary structural connections. The omitted structural cooperative relationships are: [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rejection must be preceded by form paragraph 7.30.02. Examiner must recite the omitted structural cooperative relationships and give the rationale for considering them critical or essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro Se: Narrative/Indefinite Claims (35 U.S.C. 112, 2nd para.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected as failing to define the invention in the manner required by 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph because the claim(s) are narrative in form and replete with indefinite and functional or operational language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure must be clearly and positively specified, organized and correlated to present a complete operative device. Claims must be in one-sentence form only. Examiner should note format of claims in cited patents as examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omnibus Claim (Failure to Particularly Point Out and Distinctly Claim)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, as being indefinite in that it fails to point out what is included or excluded by the claim language; this claim is an omnibus type claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rejection must be preceded by form paragraph 7.30.02. Use this paragraph to reject an 'omnibus' type claim; no further explanation is necessary. Example omnibus claim: 'A device substantially as shown and described.' See MPEP § 1302.04(b) for cancellation guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark or Trade Name as a Limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] contains the trademark/trade name [2]; where a trademark or trade name is used in a claim as a limitation to identify or describe a particular material or product, the claim does not comply with 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trademark identifies source of goods, not the goods themselves, so scope is uncertain. Insert the trademark and specify the material/product identified/ described by it (bracket instructions). Cite Ex parte Simpson. Explain why the identification/description is indefinite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate Claims (substantial duplicates)
rubrics_metrics.description: When two claims in an application are duplicates, or are so close in content that they both cover the same thing despite slight wording differences, examiner may object under 37 CFR 1.75 as being a substantial duplicate of an allowed claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraphs 7.05.05 (warning) and 7.05.06 (objection) may be used where duplicate claims are present. After allowing one claim it is proper to object to another that is a substantial duplicate. See MPEP § 706.03(k).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate Claims — Warning (Form 7.05.05)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant is advised that should claim [1] be found allowable, claim [2] will be objected to under 37 CFR 1.75 as being a substantial duplicate thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this paragraph whenever two claims are found to be substantial duplicates but are not allowable; gives applicant opportunity to correct the problem to avoid a later objection. If claims are allowable, use form paragraph 7.05.06 instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate Claims — Objection (Form 7.05.06)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] objected under 37 CFR 1.75 as being a substantial duplicate of claim [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when duplicate claims are present and objection is appropriate. If duplicate claims are not allowable, use form paragraph 7.05.05 (warning) earlier. See MPEP § 804 for double patenting and § 821–821.03 for nonelected inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: New Matter Prohibition (35 U.S.C. 132)
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment shall introduce new matter into the disclosure of the invention. Adding subject matter not disclosed in the original application (including adding specific percentages/compounds after a broader disclosure or omitting a step from a method) can constitute new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In amended cases examiner must be alert to detect new matter. Use 35 U.S.C. 132 as basis for objection to amendments to the abstract, specification, or drawings attempting to add new disclosure. If subject matter capable of illustration is originally claimed but not shown in drawing, require applicant to add it to drawings (see MPEP § 608.01(l)). If new matter is added to claims, use form paragraph 7.31.01 (35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph rejection) rather than 7.28.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objection to New Matter Added to Specification (Form 7.28)
rubrics_metrics.description: The amendment filed [1] is objected to under 35 U.S.C. 132 because it introduces new matter into the disclosure. The added material which is not supported by the original disclosure is as follows: [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant is required to cancel the new matter in reply. Do not use this paragraph in reissue applications (use form paragraph 14.22.01). In bracket 2 identify new matter by page/line numbers and/or drawing figures and provide explanation addressing any applicant statements that the matter was described as filed; include unresolved questions raising doubt as to possession at filing. If new matter affects claims, also make a 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph rejection (form 7.31.01). Treat the new matter as part of the claimed subject matter for purposes of other rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign Filing Without License (35 U.S.C. 182–185)
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing or causing filing in a foreign country prior to six months after U.S. filing, without the required license, can result in abandonment of the U.S. application or bar issuance of a U.S. patent. Licenses may be granted retroactively in limited circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If examiner learns of a corresponding foreign application filed before the U.S. application was on file six months, refer the application to Licensing and Review Section of the relevant TC (work group 3640) and call attention to the foreign filing. Pending investigation, application may be returned to the TC for prosecution on the merits. If action under 35 U.S.C. 185 is necessary, Licensing and Review will request transfer of the application. See statutory provisions for license scope and exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclaimer as Basis for Rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims may be rejected on the ground that applicant has disclaimed the subject matter involved (e.g., by failing to present claims for interference, failing to copy a claim when suggested, or failing to respond/appeal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejection on disclaimer applies to all claims not patentably distinct from the disclaimed subject matter as well as to claims directly involved. Use form paragraphs 7.48 and 7.49 for disclaimer rejections. See examples in MPEP § 706.03(u).

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure To Present Claims for Interference (Form 7.48)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. [2] based upon claim [3] of Patent No. [4]. Failure to present claims and/or take necessary steps for interference purposes after notification that interfering subject matter is claimed constitutes a disclaimer of the subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this only after applicant has been notified that interference proceedings must be instituted and applicant refused to copy the claims. In bracket 2 insert --102(g)-- or --102(g)/103(a)--. In bracket 4 insert the patent number and any additional references. When rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103(a) is used, include examiner's basis for obviousness. Note that interferences may include obvious variants (see MPEP § 2306).

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure To Appeal / Final Disposition for Interference (Form 7.49)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] stands finally disposed of for failure to reply to or appeal from the examiner's rejection of such claim(s) presented for interference within the specified time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when applicant failed to timely reply or appeal in interference-related matters. See 37 CFR 1.661 and 1.663.

rubrics_metrics.name: After Interference or Public Use Proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: The outcome of an interference or a public use proceeding may be the basis of a rejection of claims in a pending application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For rejections following an interference, see MPEP § 2363.03. Public use proceeding outcomes may provide grounds (see 37 CFR 1.292 and case law such as In re Kaslow). Notify the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences upon termination of relevant proceedings to resume prosecution or interference as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Res Judicata as Ground for Rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Res judicata may constitute a proper ground for rejection where the earlier decision was by the Board of Appeals or a reviewing court and no opportunity for further court review exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sparingly — courts have restricted res judicata rejections. Ordinarily also make rejection based on prior art, especially in continuing applications. The MPEP lists cases where res judicata rejections were sustained and cases where they were reversed; analyze claim differences, new evidence, and scope carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue Application Limitations (35 U.S.C. 251)
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 251 forbids granting a reissue enlarging the scope of the claims of the original patent unless applied for within two years from grant; reissue cannot enlarge scope after two years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such broadened claims may be rejected as barred by 35 U.S.C. 251. Reissue by assignee of entire interest permitted only when it does not enlarge scope. A defective reissue oath is ground to reject all claims in reissue application. See MPEP Chapter 1400 for reissue examination practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of Previously Allowed Claims — Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim noted as allowable shall thereafter be rejected only after the proposed rejection has been submitted to the primary examiner for consideration of all the facts and approval of the proposed action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give full faith and credit to previous examiner's search and action unless clear error or new prior art. Examiner should not take an entirely new approach or make a new search merely hoping to find something. Use Form Paragraph 7.50 when withdrawing allowability; actions that withdraw allowability require Primary Examiner signature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims Previously Allowed, Now Rejected, New Art (Form 7.50)
rubrics_metrics.description: The indicated allowability of claim [1] is withdrawn in view of the newly discovered reference(s) to [2]. Rejection(s) based on the newly cited reference(s) follow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert names of newly discovered references. Any action using this paragraph requires the signature of a Primary Examiner. Examiner Note: ensure proper insertion of references and that Primary Examiner approves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Rejection Practice (37 CFR 1.113)
rubrics_metrics.description: On the second or any subsequent examination or consideration by the examiner the rejection or other action may be made final; the examiner shall repeat or state all grounds of rejection then considered applicable and clearly state the reasons supporting them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replies to final rejection are limited (appeal or limited amendment). Before making a final rejection, develop a clear issue between examiner and applicant. If a single previous Office action contains a complete statement supporting the rejection, final may refer to it but should rebut applicant's arguments. Include Form Paragraph 7.39 to notify applicant of finality and timing. Do not make second action final if the examiner introduces a new ground of rejection not necessitated by applicant's amendment or by IDS with fee (with specific exceptions). Consider timelines, extension of time policy (37 CFR 1.136(a)), and reexamination rules when issuing final rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action Is Final — Notice and Options (Form 7.39 / 7.39.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 7.39: 'THIS ACTION IS MADE FINAL.' Notifies applicant of shortened statutory period for reply (three months) and extension policy; Form 7.39.01 provides options/requirements for pro se applicants including appeal filing and constraints on amendments after final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain shortened and maximum statutory periods, effects of filing a first reply within two months, extension fee calculation, and exceptions (not for reissue litigation or certain reexamination proceedings). For pro se: detail Notice of Appeal requirements, fees, and that amendments touching merits after final are not a matter of right unless they merely cancel claims or comply with formal requirements; show good and sufficient reasons if seeking entry of merit-touching amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Rejection Necessitated by Amendment or IDS (Form 7.40 / 7.40.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant's amendment necessitated the new ground(s) of rejection presented in the Office action, the action may be made final (Form 7.40). If an IDS filed with the fee prompted the new ground(s) of rejection, Form 7.40.01 is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When new grounds are necessitated by amendment, issue Form 7.40 and notify applicant of shortened periods per 37 CFR 1.136(a). For IDS-with-fee situations, insert the IDS filing date in bracket and use Form 7.40.01. Do not make final where the examiner has introduced another new ground of rejection not necessitated by amendment. See MPEP § 706.07(a) and related sections for when final on second action is proper.
